title: The crown prince Ismāʿīl, twenty, who ruled as regent through his father's pilgrimage, is brought home from the fleet, where he served as an admiral to carry the crown's authority over the seas, and takes the new seat in the dīwān that the Ḥijāba creates, to help his father fill the capital with scholars

data.seat: the cabinet seat added by the Ḥijāba
data.before: admiral, extending crown control over the seas (Trent)
data.task: the Emperor's scholar-building project, the seminaries and the scholars of al-Azhar (Trent)

title: A second office of the bureaucracy, inspired by the Mamlūk court and the lore of the old caliphates the Emperor met in al-Qāhira: the Ḥijāba, the chamberlainship of Umayyad Qurṭuba, whose ḥājib headed his own council, received petitioners and embassies and drafted decrees in the caliph's name. While the crown pays for it, it strengthens the crown and its legitimacy, and it gives the dīwān another seat

data.precedent: the ḥājib of the Cordoban court, raised under the caliphate of 929; under al-Manṣūr (978–1002) the office became royal power in all but name, centralising rule through the palace at the price of a nobility shut out of the caliph's counsel (the game's text)
data.date: chosen 18 January 1387 (the bureaucracy record in the save of 5 August 1395); its seat was filled on 22 January

title: Beyond the Pyrenees, Castile is losing a war it chose to join. France fell on the little county of Chiny in the Ardennes in August 1385 over trade, and Castile came in on Chiny's side with Savoy and the lords of the Rhône and the Rhineland. Two Castilian armies sent into France were destroyed, at Châteauneuf-de-Randon and at Viviers, while France keeps 40,800 men in the field

war.castileSide: defenders, with Savoy, Metz, Hainaut, Lausanne and others

source: save of 1 October 1387 (a reading); Trent's account

title: The realm whole again after the risings: 118 towns and 1,367,000 people, 557,000 of them Muslim. The game ranks al-Andalus tenth among the powers. The crown prince Ismāʿīl is married to Bernarda of Murcia, and is now counted a master of diplomacy

data.morocco: Abū al-Faḍl sultan since 7 October 1381, Jadīla queen

title: Duʿā the Marīnid, the Emperor's wife and mother of the crown prince, dies at fifty after a short illness, as the court tells it. She had sat in the dīwān for thirty-three years, under two husbands and two reigns, and ruled the court as regent through the War of the Upper March. The physicians were not summoned until the end, and the court did not ask why

data.cause: the court's account: a short illness. The game's death notice says suicide; by Trent's ruling the chronicle keeps the court's version, as with earlier deaths given out as hunting accidents and illnesses
data.roles: wife of Yūsuf I and of Saʿd; member of the dīwān from about 1355; regent 1373–1375
data.parents: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī, sultan of Fās, and Fāṭima the Ḥafṣid
data.seatLeft: her seat in the dīwān is vacant
